questions.prompt: Nothing happens when the power button is pressed: no fans, no lights. What do you check first?
choices: The wall outlet, power cord and PSU switch
questions.explanation: With no power at all, start where the power comes from and work inward.

questions.prompt: The DRAM debug LED stays lit during startup. What is the most likely cause?
choices: A memory problem, such as a badly seated module
questions.explanation: The lit LED shows the stage where startup stopped: here, memory.

questions.prompt: Fans spin but the monitor shows "No signal". Which checks make sense? Select all that apply.
choices: Plug the cable into the graphics card, not the motherboard
questions.explanation: The computer has power, so focus on display, cables, memory and graphics.

questions.prompt: Why test with a minimal configuration?
choices: It removes parts that might cause the fault, so you can add them back one by one
questions.explanation: Starting with the essentials and adding parts back reveals which part causes the problem.

questions.prompt: A PSU tester shows no output from the power supply. What should you do?
choices: Open the PSU and check the fuse
questions.explanation: A faulty PSU is replaced as a whole unit. Never open it.
